title: Legendre Symbol Characterizes Quadratic Residuosity
content: legendre_characterizes_qr is a direct application of legendreSym.eq_one_iff_isSquare from Mathlib.NumberTheory.LegendreSymbol. It says: for odd prime p and p∤a, legendreSym p a = 1 ↔ a is a square in ZMod p. This is the fundamental connection: the Legendre symbol IS the canonical isomorphism {quadratic residues mod p} → {1} and {non-residues} → {-1}, with 0 for p∣a.
mathContext: $\left(\frac{a}{p}\right) \in \{-1, 0, 1\}$. Defined via Euler's criterion: $a^{(p-1)/2} \equiv \left(\frac{a}{p}\right) \pmod{p}$. So $\left(\frac{a}{p}\right) = 1 \iff a^{(p-1)/2} = 1$ in $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z} \iff a$ is a square.
prerequisites: ZMod and its field structure for prime moduli

title: Quadratic Reciprocity in Legendre Symbol Form
content: qr_legendre is the classical quadratic reciprocity law in Legendre symbol form, proved by applying Mathlib's legendreSym.quadratic_reciprocity. For distinct odd primes p, q: (p/q)·(q/p) = (-1)^((p/2)·(q/2)) where p/2 = (p-1)/2 in integer division. This is equivalent to the standard formulation: (p/q)·(q/p) = -1 iff p ≡ q ≡ 3 (mod 4), and +1 otherwise.
mathContext: $\left(\frac{p}{q}\right)\left(\frac{q}{p}\right) = (-1)^{\frac{p-1}{2}\cdot\frac{q-1}{2}}$. The product equals $-1$ iff both $p \equiv 3$ and $q \equiv 3 \pmod{4}$. Mathlib proof via Gauss sums in $\mathbb{Z}/pq\mathbb{Z}$.
prerequisites: Natural number division for odd primes

title: First Supplement: (-1/p) = (-1)^((p-1)/2)
content: first_supplement proves (-1/p) = (-1)^((p-1)/2): -1 is a quadratic residue mod p iff p ≡ 1 (mod 4). Proved in one line using legendreSym.at_neg_one. This is the first supplement to QR and determines for which primes -1 has a square root mod p. The Hilbert symbol interpretation: (−1, p)_p = 1 iff p ≡ 1 (mod 4).
mathContext: $\left(\frac{-1}{p}\right) = (-1)^{(p-1)/2}$. For $p = 4k+1$: exponent is even, so $(-1/p) = 1$ ($-1$ is a QR). For $p = 4k+3$: exponent is odd, so $(-1/p) = -1$ ($-1$ is a non-residue).

title: Hilbert Symbol (Axiomatized)
content: The Hilbert symbol (a,b)_p = 1 iff ax² + by² = z² has a nontrivial solution in Q_p (p-adic rationals), and -1 otherwise. Axiomatized as HilbertSymbol (a b : ℤ) (p : ℕ) : ℤ because formalizing it requires: (1) Q_p as a complete non-Archimedean valued field (available in Mathlib as Padic), (2) quadratic forms over Q_p and their discriminants, (3) Hensel's lemma for lifting solutions from Z/p to Z_p.
mathContext: $(a,b)_p = 1 \iff ax^2 + by^2 = z^2$ has a nontrivial $\mathbb{Q}_p$-solution. Symmetric: $(a,b)_p = (b,a)_p$. Multiplicative: $(aa',b)_p = (a,b)_p(a',b)_p$. Product formula: $\prod_v (a,b)_v = 1$ over all places $v$ (primes $+$ $\infty$).
prerequisites: Completions of Q at prime places

title: Bridge: Jacobi → Hilbert → Class Field Theory Roadmap
content: The /-! docstring block provides a 5-level roadmap: Legendre (Mathlib, proved) → Jacobi (Mathlib, available as jacobiSym) → Hilbert (axiomatized here, requires Padic) → product formula (this IS QR in disguise, not yet formalized) → Artin reciprocity (requires class field theory, far future). This is a research survey documenting what's formalizable now and what requires future Mathlib infrastructure.
mathContext: The Jacobi symbol $J(a,n) = \prod \left(\frac{a}{p_i}\right)^{e_i}$ where $n = \prod p_i^{e_i}$. Artin reciprocity: for abelian $L/K$, the Artin map $\text{Art}_{L/K}: C_K \to \text{Gal}(L/K)$ from the idèle class group is an isomorphism. This generalizes QR ($K=\mathbb{Q}$, $L=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{a})$).
prerequisites: Jacobi symbol as product of Legendre symbols
Idèles and adèles in algebraic number theory
